sealed: Written and committed before the measuring code existed (tarpit/run.mjs, tarpit/measure.mjs, tarpit/judge.mjs) and before the tarpit was measured at its shipped settings. tarpit/measure.mjs refuses to run if this file differs from its commit, and the receipt names the commit. A claim that fails is kept as failed.
spec: Simon's tarpit organ (2026-10-28): waste, tax and harvest a confirmed attacker's own effort on our own infrastructure; never commandeer its hardware; never emit anything malicious; legit users never trapped; the separation first.
tarpit: src/tarpit.mjs (kernel, witness-gated) wired into src/server.mjs after the gate has answered: a node started with tarpit on holds a refusal only if its stage is size, magic, schema, sender, signature or recognised, the source had already been refused 500 times (the rebound ladder's top rung), and fewer than 64 refusals are held; a held refusal drips one space a second for 20 seconds, then sends the refusal exactly. Off unless the operator switches it on.
setup: One break-it node as `node run.mjs` starts it (src/server.mjs startNode), pinning the pilot's ingest key, at the tarpit's shipped settings; a twin started the same way with the tarpit off, where a claim compares. Loopback HTTP on one machine: the attacker from 127.0.0.2, genuine traffic from 127.0.0.1 unless a claim says otherwise.
attack: The attack kit's own forgery (attack-kit/forge.mjs: a well-formed message signed by a key the node does not pin), with one fixed key so every run sends the same bytes; the attacker pays the proof-of-work the shipped node asks once it has been refused 100 times (src/rebound.mjs solve). No new attack generator.
seenBefore: The wiring was smoke-tested on small settings (test/tarpit-node.test.mjs: hold 300 ms, confirm at 3, cap 2): held, answered at once past the cap, a genuine packet from the same address admitted, a source that gives up ends its hold. Nothing at the shipped settings, and none of the numbers below, has been measured.
scope: One node on one machine; the attacker and the genuine clients are local processes on loopback, not the internet. An attacker that will not wait escapes the waste quickly, though it learns nothing (p-8). Key compromise, root on the host and physical access are out; so is a flood from many addresses, which the existing rate limit and queue meet, not the tarpit. The tarpit wastes, taxes with the rebound's work, and leaves the harvest as it was; it does not make the node invulnerable.

claims.claim: Separation, another address: while the confirmed attacker is being held, the pilot's 3,000 genuine records sent from another address are all admitted, none is held, and the books equal the feed's.
claims.measure: 3,000 records from feeds/credit-default.csv (pilot packetFor) from 127.0.0.1 during the attack: admitted 3,000, held 0 (no space before any JSON; the node's held count does not move), books hash equal to the feed's

claims.claim: Separation, the attacker's own address: genuine records sent from the confirmed attacker's address are all admitted and none is held.
claims.measure: 100 genuine records from 127.0.0.2 after the attacker there is confirmed: each pays the proof-of-work the shipped node asks of that address and is admitted, 100 of 100; held 0

claims.claim: Graduated: the attacker's first 500 refusals are answered at once; from the 501st, every refused forgery is held.
claims.measure: the attacker's refusals in order: refusals 1-500 answered with no space before the JSON and none counted as held; the next 3 refused forgeries each held (20 spaces, then the refusal)

claims.claim: Waste: an attacker that sends one forgery at a time and waits for each answer completes at least ten times fewer attempts against the tarpit than against the same node with the tarpit off.
claims.measure: the confirmed attacker, one connection, sequential, paying the rebound's work, for 120 seconds against the tarpit node and for 120 seconds against the twin with the tarpit off: answers received off / on >= 10

claims.claim: Bounded: when the confirmed attacker sends 100 forgeries at once, at most 64 are held and the rest are answered at once; while 64 are held, genuine records from another address are admitted about as fast as with nothing held.
claims.measure: 100 concurrent forgeries (each with its paid work): the node's held count never exceeds 64; answers in under 5 seconds = 100 minus the number held; 200 genuine records from 127.0.0.1 while 64 are held: all admitted, median latency within 10 ms of the median of 200 sent with nothing held

claims.claim: Inert: a held answer carries the same status and the same headers as the unheld one, only spaces come before its JSON, and its JSON is byte for byte the JSON the tarpit-off twin gives for the same packet at the same point.
claims.measure: the same sequence (the attacker's 500 refusals, then 3 more forgeries) sent to both nodes: for each held answer, status equal, header names and values equal except content-length (which counts the spaces), every byte before the first '{' is 0x20, and the JSON equals the twin's byte for byte

claims.claim: Harvest unchanged: after the same attack the tarpit node has learned exactly what the tarpit-off twin learned.
claims.measure: after the p-6 sequence: the two nodes' antibody libraries are equal (exact and shape antibodies), and their journals are equal record for record with each record's time left out

claims.claim: Silence, and nothing kept: an attacker that gives up after 5 seconds receives only spaces, never a byte of the refusal, and once it has gone the node holds nothing for it.
claims.measure: a confirmed forgery whose sender closes the connection after 5 seconds: every byte received is 0x20 and there are at most 5 of them; one second later the node's held count is 0 and its abandoned count rose by 1
